l4_steps.name: Extract aircraft parts demand from MRO system
l4_steps.input: Scheduled maintenance work orders, AD compliance calendar, historical consumption rates
l4_steps.output: Parts demand list by ATA chapter, quantity, and required-by date
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥92% (actual vs planned consumption within 30-day window)
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS demand signals are not always linked to long-range MRO event schedules, causing reactive spot-buy procurement that inflates unit cost by 20–40%

l4_steps.name: Run inventory replenishment forecast in SAP MM
l4_steps.input: Current stock levels, reorder points, safety stock parameters, open POs
l4_steps.output: MRP exception report highlighting below-safety-stock and slow-moving items
l4_steps.kpi: Stockout rate ≤1.5% of demand events; safety stock coverage ≥14 days for AOG-critical parts
l4_steps.pain_point: Safety stock parameters are manually maintained and rarely updated when fleet mix changes (e.g. introduction of new variant), leading to chronic under-stocking of variant-specific parts

l4_steps.name: Review reorder triggers and approve requisition list
l4_steps.input: MRP exception report, open purchase requisitions
l4_steps.output: Approved purchase requisition batch or rejection with revised parameters
l4_steps.kpi: Requisition approval cycle time ≤4 hours for AOG-critical parts; ≤48 hours standard
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual approval queues during shift changes cause delayed AOG responses; no automated escalation when AOG-flagged requisitions remain unactioned beyond 1 hour

l4_steps.name: Create material requisition and attach technical specs
l4_steps.input: Approved purchase requisition, part number, ATA chapter, airworthiness standard (FAR/CS-25)
l4_steps.output: Sourcing-ready requisition with part description, quantity, required-by date, and certification requirements
l4_steps.kpi: Requisition completeness rate ≥98% (no return-for-correction by procurement)
l4_steps.pain_point: Part number supersession data from Boeing Toolbox is not auto-synced to SAP Ariba, causing requisitions for obsolete P/Ns that vendors cannot supply

l4_steps.name: Verify part source against Approved Vendor List
l4_steps.input: Material requisition, part number, ATA chapter
l4_steps.output: Shortlist of AVL-qualified vendors for the specific part
l4_steps.kpi: AVL coverage ≥95% of recurring part numbers; AVL review cycle ≤12 months per vendor
l4_steps.pain_point: AVL is maintained in SAP Ariba but not automatically cross-checked against FAA ASAP (Aviation Supplier Accreditation Program) suspension lists, creating compliance exposure

l4_steps.name: Validate airworthiness certification for each vendor
l4_steps.input: Vendor list, part number, applicable airworthiness directive (AD) status
l4_steps.output: Certification status decision — FAA Form 8130-3 or EASA Form 1 confirmed valid or rejected
l4_steps.kpi: Certificate validation cycle ≤2 hours; zero parts accepted without valid airworthiness release document
l4_steps.pain_point: Counterfeit parts risk is elevated for high-demand Boeing 737 consumables; manual certificate checks against FAA ACSEP database are time-intensive and inconsistently applied across stations

l4_steps.name: Issue RFQ to certified vendors via SAP Ariba
l4_steps.input: Certified vendor shortlist, technical specifications, required-by date, quantity
l4_steps.output: RFQ event published to vendors with response deadline
l4_steps.kpi: RFQ response rate ≥80% from invited vendors; RFQ-to-quote cycle ≤24 hours for standard parts, ≤4 hours for AOG
l4_steps.pain_point: AOG events require verbal quotes followed by retroactive PO creation, bypassing SAP Ariba controls and creating audit gaps under FAR Part 145 supplier documentation requirements

l4_steps.name: Evaluate vendor bids on price, lead time, and certs
l4_steps.input: Vendor quote responses including price, lead time, certification documents, warranty terms
l4_steps.output: Bid evaluation scorecard; recommended vendor selection
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiated savings vs. list price ≥8% on non-contracted parts; lead time commitment variance ≤10%
l4_steps.pain_point: Lowest-price selection without lead time weighting frequently results in late deliveries that trigger AOG events; no automated score weighting enforced in SAP Ariba evaluation templates

l4_steps.name: Create purchase order with full part traceability data
l4_steps.input: Approved vendor selection, quote reference, requisition number, delivery address
l4_steps.output: Draft PO with line items, unit price, delivery terms (INCOTERMS), and cert requirements
l4_steps.kpi: PO first-time-right rate ≥97% (no revision required post-vendor acknowledgement)
l4_steps.pain_point: INCOTERMS and hazardous material shipping codes (IATA DGR compliance for rotable parts containing hydraulic fluid) are manually entered, leading to customs clearance delays at international stations

l4_steps.name: Route PO through financial approval workflow
l4_steps.input: Draft PO, cost centre, budget availability check result
l4_steps.output: Approved or rejected PO with approval audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: PO approval cycle ≤1 business day for values ≤$50K; ≤4 hours for AOG regardless of value
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval delegation matrices in SAP FI/CO are not updated when managers are on leave, causing approval bottlenecks that delay AOG resolutions beyond IATA AHM 730 target resolution windows

l4_steps.name: Transmit approved PO and confirm vendor acknowledgement
l4_steps.output: Vendor-acknowledged PO with confirmed delivery date and tracking reference
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor acknowledgement receipt ≤4 hours of PO transmission; acknowledgement rate ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Some MRO and rotables vendors still require fax or email PO transmission; SAP Ariba supplier portal adoption is ~70%, leaving 30% of POs outside automated acknowledgement tracking

l4_steps.name: Receive parts shipment and verify packing list
l4_steps.input: Inbound shipment, vendor packing list, PO reference
l4_steps.output: Goods receipt draft with quantity discrepancy flag if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Receiving dock processing time ≤2 hours per shipment; quantity accuracy ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: AOG parts shipped via freight forwarder sometimes arrive without correct customs clearance documentation at non-hub stations, causing hold delays that negate the benefit of expedited shipping

l4_steps.name: Validate airworthiness release documents on receipt
l4_steps.input: Physical parts, FAA 8130-3 or EASA Form 1, manufacturer C of C, batch/lot traceability records
l4_steps.output: Documentation validation decision — accept, quarantine, or return to vendor
l4_steps.kpi: Documentation rejection rate ≤0.5% of line items received; zero parts accepted with missing trace-back documentation
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS certificate module does not validate 8130-3 document numbers against FAA online registry in real time; manual spot-checks miss approximately 3% of certificate anomalies per internal audit

l4_steps.name: Perform incoming quality inspection per IPC criteria
l4_steps.input: Physical parts, Illustrated Parts Catalog (IPC) criteria, AMM serviceable limits
l4_steps.output: Inspection finding report; parts tagged Serviceable, Unserviceable, or Suspect Unapproved
l4_steps.kpi: Incoming inspection pass rate ≥99.2%; suspect unapproved parts reported to FAA per AC 21-29D within 24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Tooling calibration records required for dimensional inspection are tracked in a separate CMMS that is not integrated with AMOS, creating manual cross-reference steps that slow AOG part acceptance

l4_steps.name: Accept serviceable parts to bonded stores or quarantine
l4_steps.input: Inspection finding report, serviceable tag, bin location assignment
l4_steps.output: Parts stocked in correct bin with full traceability record in AMOS; quarantine log updated for rejects
l4_steps.kpi: Bin accuracy rate ≥99.8%; quarantine disposition completed within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Bin location data in AMOS does not sync with warehouse management in SAP MM in real time, requiring nightly batch jobs that cause daytime inventory location discrepancies at high-volume line stations

l4_steps.name: Post goods receipt and update inventory in SAP MM
l4_steps.input: Accepted parts list, quantity, bin location, PO reference
l4_steps.output: GR document posted; inventory updated; open PO quantity reduced
l4_steps.kpi: GR posting lag ≤4 hours from physical acceptance; GR accuracy rate ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Back-dated GR postings to correct receiving errors distort accrual reporting in SAP FI/CO and trigger SOX compliance flags during month-end close

l4_steps.name: Execute 3-way invoice match and approve payment
l4_steps.input: Vendor invoice, PO, goods receipt document
l4_steps.output: Matched and approved invoice posted for payment; discrepancy log raised if match fails
l4_steps.kpi: 3-way match auto-approval rate ≥85%; invoice-to-payment cycle ≤30 days net; dispute resolution ≤10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Vendor invoices often include freight and handling surcharges not captured on the original PO, causing systematic 3-way match failures for ~12% of parts invoices and manual intervention by AP

l4_steps.name: Update vendor performance scorecard and close PO
l4_steps.input: Delivery performance data, quality inspection results, invoice accuracy record, lead time variance
l4_steps.output: Vendor scorecard updated; PO closed in SAP Ariba; AVL status flagged for review if score < threshold
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor scorecard completion rate ≥95% per quarter; suppliers scoring <70/100 reviewed for AVL status within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Scorecard data is manually compiled from AMOS, SAP MM, and SAP FI/CO with no automated feed; quarterly compilation takes 3–5 days and is often deprioritised during AOG-heavy periods, reducing scorecard coverage below 60%
